rules: Spelling units: letters that together spell one sound form one unit (ph, kn, ea, igh, ough, mb). A unit may spell two sounds (x is k+s, qu is k+w, le is uh+l, o in one is w+uh). A letter that has no sound and belongs to no sounding unit, like the final e in make, is its own silent unit.

kinds.ordinary: an ordinary English word, including short ones like is, by, sky
kinds.abbreviation: a shortened written form that is read aloud as the full word: Mr is read mister, Dr doctor, Jan January
kinds.initialism: initials read aloud one letter name at a time: TV, FBI, VIP, FAQ, USB
kinds.acronym: initials read aloud as one ordinary word: NASA, NATO, laser, radar
kinds.mixed: initials joined to a word part, read partly as letter names: JPEG, iPad
kinds.loan: a word borrowed from another language that keeps a foreign spelling: ballet, sushi
kinds.name: a person or place name

catalog_labels.consonant: single consonants and doubles (b, bb, ck, ...)
catalog_labels.consonant_digraph: two letters, one consonant sound (sh, ch, th, ng, ...)
catalog_labels.consonant_trigraph: three letters, one consonant sound (tch, dge, ...)
catalog_labels.consonant_silent: consonant pairs where one letter is silent (kn, wr, mb, gn, ...)
catalog_labels.consonant_combo: one spelling, two consonant sounds (x = k+s, qu = k+w, ...)
catalog_labels.vowel_digraph: two letters, one vowel sound (ai, ee, oa, ...)
catalog_labels.vowel_trigraph: three letters, one vowel sound (igh, eau, ...)
catalog_labels.vowel_quadgraph: four letters, one vowel sound (ough, augh, eigh, ...)
catalog_labels.r_controlled: vowel plus r together make ONE unit (ar, or, er, ir, ur, air, ear, ...)

kind_hint_names: The pronunciation equals the letter names said one after another
kind_pick_v2: Which kind of word is this
q_instruction: Which breakdown shows the correct spelling units of this word? Each unit is the whole letter group a reader learns as one phonogram
q_rules: Prefer the units a reader is taught as one phonogram: a vowel plus r that changes its sound is one unit (ar, or, ear, air), silent letters paired with a neighbor listed as a unit stay with it (kn, wr, mb, bt, igh), double consonants are one unit (ll, tt, ss). Otherwise use the smallest ordinary units.
